svg.data-what: the brain cut down the middle, seen from the side, the front to the left: the inner face of the hemisphere, the corpus callosum, the thalamus and hypothalamus, the brain stem and the cerebellum

g.data-what: the inner face of one cerebral hemisphere, its grey cortex folded into gyri

path.data-what: the cingulate gyrus, arching over the corpus callosum: part of the limbic system, emotion and attention
the cerebellum cut down the middle: grey cortex around white branches

g.data-what: the white matter of the cerebellum, branching like a tree (arbor vitae)
the midbrain, the top of the brain stem: eye movements, the colliculi for seeing and hearing, the substantia nigra
the pons, the bulge of the brain stem: relays between the cortex and the cerebellum, breathing rhythm

path.data-what: the medulla oblongata, the lowest part of the brain stem: breathing, heartbeat, swallowing
the top of the spinal cord, leaving the skull
the fourth ventricle, a cavity of cerebrospinal fluid between the brain stem and the cerebellum
the cerebral aqueduct, the narrow channel carrying fluid from the third to the fourth ventricle
the septum pellucidum, the thin sheet between the two lateral ventricles
the fornix, the arched bundle of fibres carrying the output of the hippocampus
the third ventricle, the narrow cavity of fluid between the two thalami
the thalamus, the relay of almost everything the senses send to the cortex
the hypothalamus: hunger, thirst, temperature, sleep, and command of the pituitary
the mammillary body, a small knob of the hypothalamus on the memory circuit
the optic chiasm, where half the fibres of each optic nerve cross to the other side

g.data-what: the pituitary gland, hanging from the hypothalamus by its stalk: the master gland of hormones

path.data-what: the pineal gland, which releases melatonin at night
the corpus callosum, the great bridge of fibres joining the two hemispheres
